When writing something that may be seen by a judge or attorneys, it is usually **better to state the legal consequence without sounding threatening or emotional**. Courts tend to take language more seriously when it is factual and procedural.

Here are a few **strong but legally appropriate ways** to say it:

**Option 1 (Most professional and court-appropriate):**  
> Failure to comply with the financial provisions outlined in our Marital Dissolution Agreement will leave me no choice but to pursue enforcement through the court, including filing a motion for contempt and seeking all remedies available under the law.

**Option 2 (Stronger but still appropriate):**  
> Continued failure to comply with the financial obligations outlined in the MDA will require me to file a motion for contempt with the court and pursue all available legal remedies to enforce the agreement.

**Option 3 (Very firm):**  
> If these obligations are not fulfilled promptly, I will proceed with filing a motion for contempt and requesting that the court impose any and all penalties and enforcement actions permitted under the law.

**Important reason to phrase it this way:**  
Courts prefer wording that says **“I will seek enforcement through the court”** rather than **“I will make sure you go to jail.”** Jail is a decision the **judge** makes, not either party.

If you'd like, I can also help you add **one final paragraph to your email that makes it legally airtight** and documents his **non-cooperation and financial obstruction**, which can matter a lot if this ever ends up in front of a judge.

**Subject: Notice of Non-Compliance With Financial Provisions of MDA**

Grant,

Your response sent on March 15, 2026 at 10:25 PM does not address the subject of my prior email, which was solely regarding the status of the transfer and release of funds and the required account closures pursuant to the terms outlined in our Marital Dissolution Agreement (MDA).

As stated in my previous email, the agreement provides a **10-day window to finalize the remaining financial matters**. Due to being scheduled for expedited surgery on Tuesday and an anticipated recovery period of several weeks, potentially up to twelve weeks, my ability to coordinate in-person banking matters during that time will be extremely limited. I therefore requested an update on the status of transferring my funds and completing the necessary account closures within the agreed timeline.

Your reply did not address these financial matters and instead contained unrelated personal communication. For clarity and documentation purposes, please note that **all communication between us must remain limited to the execution of financial obligations outlined in the MDA.** Any communication outside of those matters is inappropriate and not relevant to the required completion of the agreement.

This message serves as formal documentation that:

1. I have requested confirmation of the status of the transfer of my funds and the closure or division of the applicable accounts.
2. Your response did not address these financial obligations.
3. Access to my portion of the funds remains unresolved.

Please respond **only regarding the status of the financial transfers and account closures** so that these matters may be completed within the agreed timeframe.

If necessary, I will proceed through counsel and the court to ensure compliance with the financial provisions of the agreement.

Bethany Gifford

---
